design_context.configuration: same frozen f72e/93c8 workload images, committed-PC ROI, NpcSimTop configuration and 5ns STA corner
design_context.toolchain: local RTL simulation plus Yosys/OpenSTA mapped flow

observation.claim: f72e had 40/40 mapped Top40 paths through non-CSR serialized terminal to drain/frontend; 93c8 moved that exact target family out of Top40 with zero CPI delta and small logic-area cost, while the 5ns timing gate remained failed.

hypothesis.claim: Binding the exact memory-terminal fact to a registered exact-one serialized owner permit removes the direct terminal-to-drain/frontend Top40 path family without CPI regression.
mechanism_chain: current memory-owner terminal scalar drives the serialized drain control cone
permit D captures terminal only after registered raw backend drain and exact-one owner identity
permit Q plus owner match replaces the current terminal scalar at non-CSR drain authorization
raw backend drain and FENCE current-idle remain on the consume edge
the target terminal-to-drain/frontend path family leaves mapped Top40 while benchmark CPI remains unchanged
competing_explanations: The apparent path removal is only endpoint migration and the global critical path remains elsewhere in the terminal collector.
A configuration or source-manifest drift, rather than the RTL transform, changed the mapped path inventory.
hypothesis.falsifier: Any target non-CSR terminal-to-drain/frontend path remains in the same-design mapped Top40, CPI regresses, or owner/cancel/FENCE invariants fail.

proposal.architectural_diff: Add a valid plus 3-bit exact-one owner permit for non-CSR system, architectural trap and simulation exit; preserve current CSR eligibility, raw drain and FENCE current-idle.
preserved_invariants: serialized owner exact-one and A-to-B handoff isolation
raw backend drain remains required on consume
ROB-head trap priority and terminal side effects remain exactly once
memory token ownership and committed-store behavior are unchanged
proposal.rollback: Remove OooSerializedMemTerminalPermit and restore current mem_owner_terminalized_i as the serialized drain qualifier.

experiment.command: run-owner-timing-workload-ab.sh plus run-traceable-mapped-current.sh A1/A1b and independent reviewer inventory
experiment.repeat_reason: A1b was a distinct traceability-checker correction over the same mapped candidate; cancelled A2 is not counted as evidence.

comparison.causal_conclusion: The bounded path-family prediction is supported and CPI did not regress; this does not prove global timing closure because 93c8 still has 40/40 violations and WNS=-11.550187111 ns.

meta_critic.diagnosis: The path transform was locally causal, but the original reasoning treated edge-based cancel clearing and downstream priority as sufficient without testing an already-held permit colliding with a same-cycle high-priority cancel.

corrected_strategy.action: Separate feedback-free same-cycle kill from the complete self-consuming holder clear, gate permit readiness immediately, and test held-permit cancellation before any new PPA measurement.
corrected_strategy.scope: non-CSR serialized system/architectural-trap/simulation-exit permit under the local RV64 control plane
exceptions: CSR replay continues to use the current terminal scalar
direct frontend flush remains downstream-priority guarded because feeding it into readiness would recreate a ready/flush loop
global timing and promotion require fresh receipts for the post-fix design

reasons: 93c8 fails the exact-5ns timing hard gate
the held-cancel counterexample required a successor RTL correction
no unseen-context capability exam or system recertification exists
